gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-hk: Funky and tightly closed, Groovy hides a slit where its c nearly shuts, while Noto Sans HK lifts its brush ends and lets every curve breathe. Closed against open is what makes this pairing click.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-imperial-: Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic reads friendly and approachable, its c ending in two open pincers that never crowd the next letter. And Groovy, with its flat, unmodulated strokes, gives that openness something snug to lean against.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-inscripti: Groovy is all bounce and closed-up curves. Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian answers with big open eyes on every e and a, while the heading earns its keep when it runs large and brief.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-jp: Groovy's curves never thin out at the turns, giving the heading a friendly, marker-like roundness, while Noto Sans JP stands tall beside it. One loud voice, one level-headed one.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Noto Sans Kaithi fills its lines with big, capital-like lowercase. Groovy's loose, funky heading suits generous size, and the body text works nicely when it stays modest beside it.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Friendly describes Groovy, whose strokes look drawn with a compass pencil. It handles loud, bouncy headings well, whereas Noto Sans Kannada does its best work carrying the quieter text with gently opening s curves.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Funky is the first word for Groovy, a heading with no hairlines anywhere in its strokes. Noto Sans Kayah Li holds the text with lifted brush ends and capitals only slightly above the lowercase, which makes the two feel like opposites that agree.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-kharoshth: Noto Sans Kharoshthi lays down a thick, dark stripe of lowercase with curves that never close back on themselves. Groovy, whose joins keep their full weight where strokes meet, adds a chunky, friendly opener above that steady text.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Noto Sans Khmer reads clean and modern, with generous openings like chisel notches and small letters standing nearly capital-sized. Groovy's narrow-slit c gives the page a closed, funky counterpoint above that.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Groovy is funky and shadow-free, drawn with no hairlines at all, and Noto Sans Khojki gives it a quiet partner with wide exits and a large eye on every e. The heading brings the swagger; the body does the plain, clear talking.
